page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The system provides 12 virtual CPUs across 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 96.0 GB of memory, resulting in an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The server lacks attached local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, while network connectivity operates at a baseline speed of 2 Gbps. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AES cryptography, and BMI2.

In benchmark evaluations, single-threaded processing presents a clear performance bottleneck, with Geekbench single-core scores (930.0) and single-threaded gzip compression yielding poor results. However, multi-core scaling reaches average levels across stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests (4693.0). Uncached memory bandwidth metrics remain steady at 59.2 GB/sec for read and 49.35 GB/sec for write operations. Small model LLM inference achieves 122.96 tokens per second for text generation, but performance drops substantially on medium 7B models.

The high memory-to-vCPU allocation density offers favorable cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded clock speed or local ephemeral NVMe storage. Given its 96.0 GB RAM footprint and steady multi-threaded throughput, this instance is suitable for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, moderate relational database hosting relying on cloud storage, and batch data processing jobs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server equipped with 12 vCPUs across 6 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at 2.5 GHz and 96.0 GB of system memory. Operating on an x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it delivers a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without integrated GPU acceleration or local ephemeral storage. Network throughput features a 2 Gbps baseline. Benchmark data reflects weak single-threaded performance alongside average multi-core results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 4693.0 and Redis throughput of 8.48 million SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth maintains moderate speeds around 59.2 GB/sec for uncached reads. The combination of high memory capacity and moderate multi-threaded performance makes this instance cost-effective for in-memory caching, database operations relying on external storage, and general data processing workloads.
